title: Maiale al latte
subtitle: Pork loin braised in milk with garlic and herbs
excerpt: Maiale al latte is a northern Italian method of braising pork in milk. As the pork cooks, the milk curdles into savoury golden nuggets that cling to the meat and form the sauce. It looks unlike any other braise, but the result is pork that is exceptionally tender and a sauce of real depth.
sourceNotes: Northern Italian regional recipe. Maiale al latte is a traditional Emilian and Lombard dish. Method drawn from Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992), and Pellegrino Artusi, La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene (1891, public domain).

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice once cooled and freeze with the curdled milk sauce.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dish slices more neatly when cold. Make a day ahead and reheat slices gently.

glossaryTerms.definition: In maiale al latte, the milk is deliberately allowed to separate and brown as it reduces; the resulting golden curds cling to the pork and concentrate the flavour into a rich, slightly nutty sauce.

content.text: Maiale al latte is pork loin braised entirely in milk with garlic, sage, and lemon zest. As the pork cooks, the milk reduces and curdles into savoury golden clusters (Hazan called them the 'little golden nuggets' of the dish). The
looks unusual but tastes rich and concentrated. Do not try to prevent the milk from curdling; that is the point.

items.prepNote: enough to come two-thirds up the pork
zest only, in a single strip

content.text: Season {{pork-loin}} of pork loin all over with salt and pepper. Heat {{unsalted-butter}} of butter and {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a casserole just large enough to hold the pork. Brown the meat on all sides over medium-high heat, about 8 minutes in total. Remove.

Drain off most of the fat. Add {{garlic}} of garlic cloves, the sage, rosemary, and lemon zest. Cook for 1 minute. Return the pork. Pour in enough {{whole-milk}} of warm milk to come two-thirds up the meat. Bring to a very gentle simmer.

Braise over low heat, partially covered, for 1 hour 20 minutes, turning the pork every 20 minutes. The milk will curdle and reduce to small golden clusters by the end. If the pan dries out before the pork is done, add a little more milk. Rest 10 minutes. Slice and serve with the pan sauce spooned over.

items.symptom: Milk did not curdle into golden clusters
items.cause: Heat too low, or braising time too short.
items.fix: Remove the lid and increase the heat slightly for the final 20 minutes. The milk needs to evaporate and brown.

items.cause: Cooked at too high a temperature or for too long after the internal temperature was reached.
items.fix: Loin is lean; don't go past 70°C at the centre. Use a probe thermometer.

content.text: Maiale al latte is associated with Emilia-Romagna and Lombardy, where pork is the dominant meat and dairy is abundant. The technique of braising in milk has been used in northern Italy for centuries and appears in several of Artusi's recipes. Hazan described it as one of the best pork preparations in the Italian repertoire. The curdled appearance alarms some cooks; once they taste the sauce, the alarm passes.
